events.title: Joseph weeps over his dead father
events.narrative_summary: Joseph falls on his father's face, weeps over him and kisses him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediately after Jacob's death (49:33), so anchored on its END with no delay; an hour for the farewell, margin an hour.

events.title: Joseph's physicians embalm Israel
events.narrative_summary: Joseph commands his servants the physicians to embalm his father, and they do so; forty days are completed, as is the custom for the embalmed.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The command follows the weeping (anchor: its END). 'Forty days' (50:3) is the stated duration; Radak and Rashi take 40 as the embalming. Margin one day for the command's start.

events.title: Egypt mourns Jacob seventy days
events.narrative_summary: The Egyptians weep for Jacob seventy days.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Seventy days counted from the death (anchor: Jacob's death, START), so the 40 days of embalming lie inside it; Rashi and Radak say 40 for embalming and 30 more for weeping. Margin one day.

events.title: Joseph asks Pharaoh's leave to bury his father
events.narrative_summary: When the days of weeping are past, Joseph asks Pharaoh's household to speak for him: his father made him swear to bury him in Canaan. Pharaoh grants it.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'The days of his weeping passed' (50:4): starts when the seventy days end (anchor: the mourning, END), no further delay. One day for message and reply, margin two days.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: When the days of his weeping had passed

events.title: Egypt's elders and chariots go up with Joseph
events.narrative_summary: Joseph goes up to bury his father with all Pharaoh's servants and the elders of Egypt, his household and brothers, chariots and horsemen; only the children and flocks stay in Goshen. The company is very great.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Departs after Pharaoh's leave (anchor: the petition, END). Goshen to Atad: ~465 km by road. I pace it on foot, ≈ 16 days (urim travel walk, 4 km/h, about 28 km a day), because the company is 'very great' (kaved, 50:9) with elders and a household, and the chariots (gam, 'also') escort rather than set the pace. Chariots alone would take ≈ 7 days; margin 3 days covers a somewhat faster march.

events.title: A great lament at the threshing floor of Atad
events.narrative_summary: At the threshing floor of Atad beyond the Jordan they hold a great and heavy lament, and Joseph keeps seven days of mourning. The Canaanites see it and name the place Abel-mizraim.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Begins on arrival at Atad (anchor: the procession, END); the text gives seven days of mourning, hence duration 7 days, margin one day.

events.title: Jacob's sons bury him at Machpelah
events.narrative_summary: His sons do as he commanded: they carry him to Canaan and bury him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, east of Mamre.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: After the seven days at Atad (anchor: the lament, END) the sons carry him on to Machpelah: ~74 km by road, chariot 12 km/h, ≈ 1 day (urim travel), so offset 1 day. A few hours for the burial; margin a day.

events.title: Joseph and all who went up return to Egypt
events.narrative_summary: After burying his father, Joseph returns to Egypt with his brothers and all who had gone up with him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'After he had buried his father' (50:14): anchor the burial, END. Machpelah to Goshen by chariot: ~403 km by road, 12 km/h, ≈ 6 days (urim travel); margin two days.

events.title: Joseph's brothers fear him and plead for pardon
events.narrative_summary: Seeing that their father is dead, the brothers fear Joseph will repay their evil. They send word that Jacob commanded him to forgive them, and then come and fall before him as his servants; Joseph weeps.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The fear arises 'when they saw that their father was dead'; no interval is stated, so it is placed right after the return (anchor: the return, END) with a one-month margin. No time word: MACRO_ERA.

events.title: Joseph tells his brothers not to fear
events.narrative_summary: Joseph tells them not to fear: he is not in God's place, what they meant for evil God meant for good, to keep many alive. He promises to provide for them and their little ones and comforts them.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Direct reply to the brothers' plea (50:19), so anchored on its END; a speech of about half an hour.

events.title: Joseph lives on in Egypt and sees his great-grandchildren
events.narrative_summary: Joseph stays in Egypt with his father's household and lives 110 years. He sees Ephraim's children of the third generation, and the sons of Machir son of Manasseh are born on his knees.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Runs from the reassurance until his death at 110 (50:22, 26). Jacob died when Joseph was about 56 on the Masoretic chain, so about 54 years remain; margin one year.

events.title: Joseph tells his brothers God will bring them up
events.narrative_summary: Joseph tells his brothers he is dying, that God will visit them and bring them up to the land sworn to the patriarchs, and has the sons of Israel swear to carry up his bones.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Joseph is 110 at his death (50:26): offset 110 years from anchor.joseph_birth, margin a year (an age covers the whole year), REGNAL_YEAR. An hour for the speech and oath.
events.ancient_year_marker: At a hundred and ten years

events.title: Joseph dies at 110 and is put in a coffin in Egypt
events.narrative_summary: Joseph dies at 110. They embalm him and he is put in a coffin in Egypt.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows his last words (anchor: END); the text gives no interval before death or for the embalming. Duration 40 days is the embalming, which 50:3 gives as the custom ('so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed'); 50:26 says 'they embalmed him'. Margin 5 days for how long the embalming ran; the 70 days of Egypt's weeping are not applied to him. Tier REGNAL_YEAR: his age at death.
events.ancient_year_marker: A hundred and ten years old

causal_edges.causal_explanation: His sons bury him 'as he commanded them' (50:12), according to his charge in 49:29–32.
Jacob's charge and oath to be buried at Machpelah is what Joseph asks Pharaoh to let him fulfil (50:5).
Seeing their father dead, the brothers fear Joseph's revenge and plead for pardon (50:15).
Jacob's death prompts Joseph to have him embalmed for the journey to Canaan (50:2).
Jacob's death leads Joseph to fall on his face, weep and kiss him (50:1).
Their plea and self-surrender draw Joseph's reply, 'Fear not' (50:19).
Pharaoh's leave, 'Go up and bury your father' (50:6), makes the journey possible, and 50:7 follows it.
